features.feature_value: Used the pair to detect identical aggressive/insulting phrasing and focused on harassment/dehumanization over politics
features.evidence_span: Evaluating them as a pair made it easier to spot when both sides used the exact same aggressive or insulting phrasing
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes using the paired comparison to find hostile language patterns rather than political viewpoint differences.

features.feature_value: Decided based on whether it fit free speech or hate rhetoric
features.evidence_span: if it was free speech or hate rhetoric
features.rationale: They state the exact decision criterion they used to evaluate the post as a pair.

features.feature_value: Removed when misinformation, excessive inflammation, or lack of contribution
features.evidence_span: mainly removed the comment if it stated misinformation, was excessively inflammatory or did not contribute
features.rationale: Their reflection lists specific removal triggers that guided moderation decisions.

features.feature_value: Omitted comments that were angry or vulgar and lacked constructive conversational value
features.evidence_span: simply angry or vulgar in their comments, and had nothing constructive added
features.rationale: They directly connect “angry/vulgar” with “nothing constructive” as the basis for omitting.

features.feature_value: Disliked curse words as feeling unnecessary at that moment
features.evidence_span: didn't really like the ones with the curse words, it just felt unnecessary for those to be there at that moment
features.rationale: They describe a subjective negative reaction to profanity shaping their moderation/selection.

features.feature_value: Accepted both when most of each post was well-stated and mostly objective; otherwise rejected when intentionally crude/insulting
features.evidence_span: If most of each post was well-stated and mostly objective, I chose to accept both
features.rationale: They set a comparative rule about crudeness/insults versus objectivity to decide accept/omit.

features.feature_value: Chose options that appeared to represent diversified views on both sides
features.evidence_span: looked like they had a diversified view of both sides in my decision making
features.rationale: They describe using balanced representation across the pair to guide their choices.

features.feature_value: Felt they would actually engage with the posts; this positive engagement made the survey pleasing
features.evidence_span: I felt as If these posts were posts that I would actually engage in
features.rationale: Their influence appears driven by anticipated engagement and positive feelings rather than explicit moderation rules.
